GROSS/NET POWER, KW 170/99 WINTER SEASON NET POWER KW/HP 68/91 PEAK SEASON NET POWER KW/HP 130/175 4.2.1.1 Considerations, Advantages and Disadvantages As mentioned above, locating the OTEC equipment inside of the hull column provides maximum protection from storm damage. With this configuration, all of the equipment would be located inside the hull, except for the penetrations in the hull column necessary for access of the cold- and warm-water intake pipes as well as water discharge. Two penetrations in the bottom of the hull column allow the cold water pipe to enter, and the warm water outlet pipe to exit. The penetrations in the side of the hull column allow the warm water pipe to enter and the cold water outlet pipe to exit. In this configuration, the penetrations in the side of the hull column would be more susceptible to storm damage because they may be located in the wave zone, and additional reinforcement and/or locating them on the inner side of the hull column. Since there is equipment (such as ballast pumps and other utility equipment) that is installed in one or more of the hull columns on a typical oil and gas semi-submersible platform, there are already instrument cables and power cables routed from the operational deck (or the “topsides”) into the hull column(s). The addition of the OTEC equipment will require additional power lines and instrument cables to tie the OTEC equipment into the power system and the control system. Integrating the OTEC facility into a new oil and gas platform affords the opportunity to design the ballast system and account for the additional weight (approximately 41 metric tons per hull column) in the original design. An advantage of locating the equipment inside the hull column, in addition to being provided maximum storm protection, is that it helps to lower the overall center of gravity of the platform, which potentially aids in the platform’s stability. 9 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 One disadvantage of locating the OTEC equipment inside the hull column is that maintenance of the equipment can be more challenging due to accessibility limitations. As presented in the Objective 2 report, the modeled OTEC system requires heat exchangers to be located no higher than 30 feet above the sea level, and it requires that the refrigerant pump be located below the condenser. It is envisioned that the turbine generator would be above the evaporator and condenser. With these different elevations, there are likely to be equipment “levels” inside the hull column, with stairs or ladders between them. Provisions for cleaning the heat exchangers in place or removing the heat exchangers for maintenance, repair, or replacement should be considered in the design.
